summary: The prepared base already contains the issue-specific correction. Req.update_finish_state checks invalid-token, stop-string, and stop-token finishes before max_new_tokens, then _cap_finished_len_at_max_new_tokens demotes only stops beyond the budget. The exact six-token issue replay finishes as FINISH_MATCHED_STR at finished_len=3 and emits [10, 11, STOP]. Upstream PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33758 merged the effective fix as b2f9603f93ea8ee3f921557c95e5a8c4c3ce720a; the issue-referenced PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31569 remains open.

tests.what_was_measured: Real Req.update_finish_state behavior for the reported in-budget stop plus independent exact-cap, beyond-cap, and no-stop overshoot boundaries; all four assertions passed. Raw output: reports/j-cce585271080/raw/replay_issue_31599.txt

Twenty real scheduler unit tests covering speculative stop/EOS versus length precedence, post-EOS bonus-token trimming, stop beyond budget, exact-cap ties, no-stop length finish, grammar stop boundaries, and stop-string/regex chunk boundaries. Raw output: reports/j-cce585271080/raw/focused_pytest.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: The defect and fix are deterministic CPU-side Req.update_finish_state ordering and output slicing. The replay and registered tests execute the real method without launching a GPU kernel. No model weights or serving-path run was used, so no GPU, model-semantic, or distributed-workload claim is made.

remaining_limitations: No full model-serving or speculative-decoding engine run was performed; the evidence directly exercises the production request finish-state implementation with deterministic token chunks.
No GPU numerical result is relevant to this Python control-flow defect, and none is claimed.
Because the prepared base was already fixed, this PR adds investigation artifacts and an executable replay rather than changing production source.
